Like Tagalog, Cebuano uses TWO number systems (data/style.md): native for
counting things and people, Spanish-derived for clock time and prices. A
counting picture carries one production per quantity (`values` must be
injective after `exclude`), and counting is the NATIVE context.
usa      — 'one' AND the indefinite article (usa ka bata = a child), the
same reasoning as tl `isa` and no `en`.
the Spanish-derived words — their context is a clock face or a price.
Teens are multi-word (napulo'g usa = 11) and so are not single tokens; they
are omitted rather than listed in a form no headword takes.
